problem:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the function given below?

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}, & x\ne 1 \\ 2, & x=1\end{aligned}
$$

- It is continuous and differentiable at $x=1$
- It is **not** continuous at $x=1$ but it is differentiable at $x=1$
- It is **not** differentiable on the interval $x\in (-2,2)$
worked_solution:
Let's analyze each statement individually.

- Statement I is false. First, we investigate the continuity of $f(x)$ . It is continuous everywhere except, possibly, $x=1.$ At this point, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}{x}^{2}={1}^{2}=1 \\ {lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}{x}^{2}={1}^{2}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to {1}^{+}}f(x)={lim}_{x\to {1}^{-}}f(x)\ne f(1)=2,
$$

and so $f(x)$ is not continuous at $x=1$ (it is a removable discontinuity).

- Statement II is false. Since $f(x)$ is not continuous at $x=1,$ it is also not differentiable there.

- Statement III is true. Since $f(x)$ is not differentiable at $x=1,$ it is not differentiable on any interval that includes this point. Consequently, it is not differentiable in $x\in (-2,2).$

Therefore, only statement III is true.
